correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern opening and northward receiving headwater
correspondence.finding: The municipal and geological originals depict the headward north-running drainage that receives the selected opening, its small side branches and its continuous northward course toward the eastward Cunani bend. The short initial west-to-east stored stub lies slightly west of the drawn headwater line. The identification of this stub with the immediate headwater receiving corridor is an ordinary-scale geographic inference from the surrounding mapped drainage, not a claim that every initial segment is explicitly drawn or surveyed. No distinct-basin crossing, lake-to-feeder transfer or managed connector is indicated. A separate name for the chosen initial feeder is not established.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward upper bend and northeast approach to Carnot
correspondence.finding: Both cartographic originals show the upper drainage turning east and then northeast into the reach directly labeled Rio Cunani. Its bends, several small lateral joins and continuous approach to the BR-156/Carnot corridor correspond to the selection. The name is attached to this receiving river; it is not assigned independently to each small joining stream.

correspondence.component_scope: Carnot road crossing and north/northeast middle river
correspondence.finding: The original maps follow the same river through the Carnot/Agrovila do PA Carnot road-crossing setting and north-northeast through the forested interior, with its intermediate tributary joins and turns. The park plan independently places Carnot beside Rio Cunani and BR-156. There is no necessary lake, reservoir or engineered passage along this selected interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward lower-middle bends, Cunani village and approach to the stage boundary
correspondence.finding: The river turns east through increasingly sinuous lower-middle bends to Vila Cunani and continues east beyond it. The municipal original covers all stored fragment-end parts, while the geological original corroborates the river/village relationship and the adjacent tributary network. Igarapé Mocambo and Rio Novo are separately labeled lateral waters, not aliases of the main river. The management plan independently associates Cunani village with Rio Cunani and describes historical tidal influence in this lower setting.

correspondence.component_scope: Stage-3/stage-2 continuation and southeast-directed lower bends
correspondence.finding: The municipal original depicts a continuous river across the fragment join, from the Cunani/Vila União locality setting past the river-side settlements into the southeastward lower bends. The change of stored stage does not correspond to a change of receiving basin or a newly named main river. Several small mapped lateral drainage joins remain distinct from the selected mainstem.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward widened lower river and coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The municipal original directly labels Rio Cunani on the eastward widened lower reach and shows its connected bends toward the Atlantic coast. The selected southern turn, eastward interval and final northeastward approach occupy this same fluvio-estuarine corridor. The historical park-plan prose corroborates the named river, village and mouth relationship. This does not establish present tides, discharge, navigation or exact banks.

correspondence.component_scope: Final Cunani-mouth reach and separate source/render ending contexts
correspondence.finding: The municipal original shows the final lower bend opening directly to the Atlantic coastal receiving water. The stored source ending falls in the generalized river-mouth/coastal-margin setting near the southern side of the opening. The render ending is displaced northeast toward the northern coastal side of that same mouth. These are separately retained ordinary receiving-geography descriptions, not claims that either coordinate is a surveyed bank or lies within the contemporary wetted channel. No farther downstream river, separate lagoon or tidal shortcut is appended.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen upper wash and western bend
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is in the branching foothill drainage southeast of Laguna de Arriba and north of the principal Sierra Encinillas relief. The selected wash bends west and northwest, then southwest into the receiving bajada on the western side of the range. The lake labeled Laguna de Arriba is a separate nearby waterbody; its label is not evidence that the selection crosses that lake.

The route follows the southward mapped drainage and continuous sloping receiving floor west of Sierra Encinillas, with short side washes entering from the range and western terrain. This is a mapped ordinary corridor, without a required continuously wet channel.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward turn onto the southern plain
correspondence.finding: After the southern bend the selected drainage turns east across the foot of the range. Mapped watercourses and the common alluvial receiving floor establish the turn and the eastward connection; nearby southwest drainage toward Laguna El Gigante is kept separate.
correspondence.name_scope: No name transferred from the neighboring lake or other western reaches.

correspondence.finding: The selected central lowland corresponds to the waterbody and receiving floor directly labeled Laguna Texcoco. Its western approach and eastward continuation are both mapped in the same low-gradient plain, with several separate north-side mountain washes joining.
correspondence.name_scope: Laguna Texcoco is a bounded lake/lowland name, not a whole-river candidate.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern receiving plain and tributary joins
correspondence.finding: The eastward route continues across the mapped plain below Sierra Encinillas, receiving multiple separately drawn northern washes and a southern branch in the Los Pilares vicinity. The name Los Pilares is printed along that southern feeder, not along the complete selected eastward route. The continuous mapped receiving corridor supports correspondence through the small stored parts and joins.
correspondence.name_scope: Los Pilares remains a separate tributary name; no whole-composite alias relationship is supported.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastern bend and return toward Laguna Jaco
correspondence.finding: The selected continuation bends southeast across the same lowland and then northeast into the broader Laguna Jaco receiving-floor setting south of Cerro Gordo. The mapped channels, plain and adjoining bajada support this broad direction change without a separate-basin or missing lake-to-feeder transfer.

The final southeastward and southward segments enter the lake/playa-floor setting directly labeled Laguna Jaco. The short final stored part ends within that terminal receiving setting. The generalized map supports the basin correspondence without deciding an exact historical shoreline side or present open-water position.
correspondence.name_scope: Laguna Jaco is the bounded terminal waterbody/basin name, not a river name.

correspondence.finding: The selected southern opening is within elongated lake-rich terrain. Its northward then northwestern course encounters several small waterbodies and shallow connecting depressions. The original image establishes this setting but does not resolve every lake-to-feeder transfer.
correspondence.uncertainty: Names of the opening waterbodies and actual through-link remain unsupported; the selected model line is not evidence of flow between them.

correspondence.finding: West-leading water and valley features provide ordinary geographic correspondence through the middle selection, including an elongated lake and a river corridor farther west.
correspondence.uncertainty: This generalized corridor observation does not establish a whole-composite natural-river name or the upstream lake transfers.

correspondence.finding: The selected route turns into and continues along a visibly incised, meandering northwestern river valley. The main valley itself continues northwest beyond the point where the selection later turns away.
correspondence.uncertainty: Nearby Inman coastal prose is not sufficient by itself to assign a name to all inland segments.

correspondence.component_scope: river to separate lake trough transfer
correspondence.finding: The selection turns northeast out of the established river valley toward a separate north-leading lake trough. Readable imagery does not establish a receiving channel or continuous ordinary valley connecting these systems across the intervening terrain.
correspondence.uncertainty: This is the primary substantive material gap. No interbasin transfer, lake outlet reversal or current water movement is inferred.

correspondence.finding: The subsequent selection follows the vicinity of elongated northern lakes and small interposed low areas. Their geographic placement is visible; the lake-to-feeder connections needed to join the previous river valley to the coastal stream remain unestablished.
correspondence.uncertainty: Lake outlines alone do not establish through-flow or continuity across the previous transfer.

correspondence.finding: The final part approaches the south coast of Dolphin and Union Strait through a small coastal drainage setting east of the Inman River mouth described in the independently read sailing directions. The stored source endpoint is in the coastal outlet setting; the rendered endpoint is a separate, slightly landward position. Neither is replaced with the nearby named Inman mouth.
correspondence.uncertainty: A local mouth setting does not establish the missing inland through-link, a literal sea point for each stored endpoint, or a river name.

correspondence.finding: The selection begins within a dissected southeastern headward tributary area. Convergent shallow rills and the adjoining tributary-valley floor provide ordinary receiving-corridor correspondence to the northwestern drainage. The initial turn is retained as stored rather than moved onto a particular visible rill.
correspondence.uncertainty: No separate upper-feeder name or exact active opening channel is established.

correspondence.finding: The westward then northwestern upper selection lies within the connected tributary-valley approach to the larger incised receiving corridor. Tributaries from both sides visibly converge on that corridor.
correspondence.uncertainty: Generalized terrain and valley connection, without a claim that every modeled vertex lies on a present wet thread.

correspondence.finding: The route continues northwest through the incised river corridor, with tributary ravines and successive bends visible in the original image. No intervening lake or separate basin transfer is required.
The same connected valley extends north then northwest through the middle selection. Multiple side ravines enter the corridor while its main receiving direction remains continuous.
correspondence.uncertainty: Names of side tributaries remain null; no legal name boundary is inferred.

correspondence.finding: The main corridor continues toward the northwestern coast, receiving side valleys and widening downstream. The large visible western and eastern branches remain distinguishable from the selected through-corridor.
correspondence.uncertainty: Ordinary drainage continuity is established without exact bank alignment or present discharge.

correspondence.finding: The valley opens into a broad alluvial delta at the head of Cunningham Inlet, matching the independently read CHS description of Cunningham River. The stored source endpoint and the slightly farther north rendered endpoint occupy distinct positions in the same delta/inlet-edge receiving setting; neither is substituted with another distributary mouth.
correspondence.uncertainty: The precise tidal/freshwater boundary and currently active distributary at either endpoint are unestablished and are not needed for ordinary delta correspondence.
